items.title: What's Hot, What's Not: AI Search Changes In Q1 2026 [Recap]
items.summary: This Search Engine Journal article recaps the key developments in AI search during the first quarter of 2026, highlighting what's gaining traction and what's fading. It covers shifts in generative engines, optimization techniques, and their impact on SEO strategies. Marketers are urged to adapt quickly to maintain visibility in evolving AI-driven search landscapes.

items.title: Google March 2026 Core Update: What Agencies Need to Know and How to Recover
items.summary: Google's March 2026 Core Update is affecting websites, with agencies needing to prioritize quality content and integration of GEO practices. The update emphasizes E-E-A-T signals and user experience improvements for recovery. SEO professionals are advised to audit sites and adjust strategies promptly.

items.title: Google Algorithm Updates March 2026: Complete Guide for SEO Agencies
items.summary: A detailed guide on Google's March 2026 algorithm changes, focusing on impacts to SEO and content marketing. It provides actionable steps for agencies to navigate volatility, including enhanced GEO and AI optimization. Emphasis is placed on adapting to new ranking factors for sustained performance.

items.title: RumoredAI Launch: Audit & Fix AI Hallucinations for Brands (GEO/AEO Tool)
items.summary: Josh Pigford introduces RumoredAI, a new tool that reveals what AI models say about your brand, spots hallucinations, benchmarks against competitors, and offers prioritized fixes with copy-paste prompts. It's designed for AEO/GEO optimization without ongoing subscriptions, starting at $25 with dynamic pricing. Early testers report mind-blowing insights for brand visibility in AI search.

items.title: 93% of AI Search Sessions End Without Website Visits – GEO & AEO Take Over
items.summary: Scott warns that traditional SEO is obsolete as 93% of AI search users never visit sites, pushing the need for GEO and AEO in 2026. He outlines recent monthly changes in AI search dynamics driving zero-click results. Brands must pivot to be cited in AI summaries for visibility.

items.title: The Old Game Is Over: GEO is the New Standard for Search in 2026
items.summary: Gazi Masud declares traditional SEO ending due to AI overviews causing 'Great Decoupling' – rising impressions but falling clicks. He introduces GEO as key, stressing proprietary data, semantic depth, and multi-platform presence. Shares a 2026 checklist including AI citation optimization and human-centric content.

items.title: Grammarly Removes AI 'Expert Review' Feature After Backlash Over Mimicking Writers
items.summary: Grammarly has removed its AI Expert Review feature, which generated editing suggestions inspired by prominent writers like Stephen King and academics such as Neil deGrasse Tyson without consent. The move followed backlash from authors, including a class-action lawsuit claiming over $5m in damages for misusing identities. CEO Shishir Mehrotra apologized, announcing a redesign amid criticisms from living and deceased figures' representatives.

items.title: Nearly 10,000 Authors Publish Empty 'Don't Steal This Book' to Protest AI Theft
items.summary: Nearly 10,000 authors, including Jacqueline Wilson and Kazuo Ishiguro, released the mostly empty 'Don't Steal This Book' to protest AI companies training on their works without permission or payment. Organized by Ed Newton-Rex, it urges the UK government to protect copyright amid plans to ease AI access, with blank pages symbolizing threats to livelihoods. 1,000 free copies are distributed at London Book Fair.

items.title: AI Supercharges Scams Targeting Self-Published Authors
items.summary: Fraudsters from south Asia and Africa use AI to personalize scams promising self-published authors bestseller status, reviews, and fake deals, as seen in Jon Cocks' A$10,000 loss on unusable trailers and prints. With self-publishing surging past traditional output, scams offer illegal reviews and impersonate firms like Barnes & Noble. Authorities and groups like Australian Society of Authors warn of the AI-fueled boom.

items.title: Grammarly's AI 'Expert Review' Cosplays Real Writers Without Permission
items.summary: Ellipsus details Grammarly's Expert Review feature using AI to generate advice mimicking authors like Stephen King without permission, calling it a grift with poor quality output. The thread criticizes writing tools pivoting to enshittified AI, betraying user trust. Feature removed after backlash.

items.title: 10,000 Authors Release Empty Book Protesting AI Theft of Work
items.summary: Ed Newton-Rex announces 'Don't Steal This Book', a mostly empty publication by almost 10,000 authors protesting AI theft amid UK copyright changes favoring AI firms. Blank pages represent impact on livelihoods; 1,000 free copies at London Book Fair. Full list at dontstealthisbook.com.

items.title: OpenAI's GPT 5.4 Guardrails Cripple Creative Writing
items.summary: Kenshii_ai slams GPT 5.4's stricter guardrails blocking human-like emotion, tension, and storytelling, rendering it unusable for creative writing. OpenAI's escalating censorship on its strongest model prioritizes nannybot restrictions over utility for writers. Examples show refusals for natural narrative elements.

items.title: Oscars 2026: 'One Battle After Another' Wins Best Picture
items.summary: Paul Thomas Anderson's 'One Battle After Another' won the Best Picture Oscar at the 98th Academy Awards on March 15, 2026. The film also secured Best Director for Anderson. The ceremony featured numerous highlights including emotional tributes and major wins.

items.title: Oscars 2026 Best and Worst Moments
items.summary: The 97th Academy Awards hosted by Conan O'Brien included standout wins for Michael B. Jordan and Amy Madigan. Rolling Stone recaps the best, worst, and most surprising moments from Hollywood's biggest night. Historic achievements marked the event.

items.title: Hollywood's Woke Jokes Flop at the Oscars
items.summary: Woke-themed jokes at the 2026 Oscars reportedly fell flat with audiences. A YouTube segment critiques the handling of such content in culture, sports, news, and media. Hosts discuss the biggest stories unfiltered.

items.title: Rachel Zegler Calls Snow White Backlash 'Really Confusing'
items.summary: Rachel Zegler expressed confusion over audience backlash to Disney's Snow White remake, stating 'I refuse to assimilate for anybody else's comfort.' The comments appear in a Variety interview shared widely on X. Fans have criticized changes to the classic tale.

items.title: Liberals Call for Shrek Boycott Over Pro-Deportation Scenes
items.summary: Social media users on the left are urging a boycott of Shrek after clips resurfaced showing scenes interpreted as pro-deportation. Posts mock the calls as overreach on the classic animated film. The reaction highlights polarized audience responses to content.

items.title: Timothée Chalamet Draws Backlash for Dismissing Ballet and Opera
items.summary: Timothée Chalamet sparked uproar by stating 'no one cares' about ballet and opera. Josh Groban called the reaction 'accidentally positive,' boosting arts discussion during Oscars coverage. CNN shared the update on the entertainment controversy.

items.title: Intuit Launches AI-Powered ERP Solution for Small Construction Businesses
items.summary: Intuit introduced a new AI-powered ERP system tailored specifically for the construction industry, targeting small businesses. The tool streamlines operations, enhances productivity, and addresses sector-specific challenges. This marks a significant product move to bring practical AI to SMBs.

items.title: BytePlus Unveils Seedream 5.0 Lite for Real-World E-commerce AI Creation
items.summary: BytePlus launched Seedream 5.0 Lite, an AI tool that generates high-quality product visuals and campaign creatives for e-commerce from simple inputs. It combines reasoning with multimodal generation to enable faster, smarter content creation for brands. Ideal for small businesses seeking practical AI for sales and marketing.

items.title: Stripe-Led Tempo Blockchain Goes Live with Protocol for AI Agents
items.summary: Stripe-backed payments blockchain Tempo launched, featuring a protocol specifically for AI agents to handle transactions. This platform move positions it as key infrastructure for AI-driven businesses and agents. Signals intensifying competition in AI-integrated payment systems for small businesses.
